label: Fourier embedding of the noise level
context: Explains AlphaFold 3's Fourier embedding of the noise level. Use a fixed seeded random generator: draw 12 frequencies w_k ~ Normal(0,1) and 12 phases b_k ~ Normal(0,1) once. Horizontal axis: u = (1/4) ln(sigma / 16), drawn from u = -2.1 to 1.4, with tick labels showing sigma in angstrom (0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000) at u = 0.25*ln(sigma/16). Upper panel: the 12 curves cos(2*pi*(w_k*u + b_k)) as 12 thin stacked horizontal strips (one small wave each), slow waves for small |w_k|, fast waves for large |w_k|. A vertical rust cursor sweeps slowly from sigma = 2560 (u = 1.27) down to sigma = 0.0064 (u = -1.96), like a sampler going from noise to data. Lower panel: the current embedding n_k = cos(2*pi*(w_k*u + b_k)), k = 1..12, as 12 vertical bars (blue positive, rust negative) that change smoothly as the cursor moves; a label shows the current sigma in angstrom. Phase 1 caption 'u = 1/4 ln(sigma / sigma_data): a log scale, so 2560 A and 0.006 A fit on one short axis'. Phase 2 caption 'each feature is a wave in u with its own random frequency w_k and phase b_k'. Phase 3 caption 'the values at the cursor are the code the network receives (256 of them in AF3)'. Phase 4: freeze two cursors at sigma = 10 A and sigma = 20 A and show both bar codes side by side (similar), then sigma = 10 A and sigma = 100 A (clearly different); caption 'a factor 2 apart: similar codes; a factor 10 apart: nearly unrelated codes'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 420 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas. Loop forever on a cycle of 16 to 22 s with smooth easing. White background. Ink #04204B, blue #0B4FC0, rust #B4552F. One-line phase caption at the top centre. No title inside the canvas. Plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: How the noise level becomes a code of 256 numbers
spec.caption: A log-scaled noise axis u, twelve random Fourier waves, and the vector of wave values at the cursor that the network receives.
